tip: In goodbyes, nog adds 'for the rest of', so Prettige avond nog wishes you a good remainder of the evening.
Say tot plus a time to mean 'see you then': tot snel is 'see you soon'.
Start with a time word and the verb comes next, before the subject: Overmorgen vertrekken wij, not Overmorgen wij vertrekken.
Motion into something wraps the noun in tegen ... in: tegen de wind in means straight into the wind.
For a route Dutch uses lopen (to run or go), so het pad loopt langs de rivier means the path runs along the river.
Dutch names the posture instead of using 'is': an upright object staat, so de stoel staat bij de tafel.
For a future span, over means 'in': over twee weken is 'in two weeks', counting forward from now.
nooit (never) follows the verb: Wij eten nooit vlees, not Wij nooit eten vlees.
Passive uses worden plus a past participle: wordt verstuurd means 'is being sent'.
aanraden is a splitting verb: the aan detaches to the end, so raadt de dagschotel aan means recommends it.
geleden (ago) comes after the time span: tien jaar geleden means 'ten years ago'.
With sinds, Dutch stays in the present tense: Sinds vorig jaar woon ik means I have lived since last year.
The -je ending makes a small or countable version: snoep is candy in general, snoepjes are individual sweets.
After dat the verb moves to the very end, so in dat alles goed zou komen the words zou komen close the clause.
als with a past tense means 'whenever' for a repeated action: als het regende is 'whenever it rained'.
Regular past adds -te or -de to the stem: bak plus te gives bakte, meaning 'baked'.
zitten covers something lodged in place: de sleutel zit in het slot means the key is in the lock.
pas means 'not until': Wij eten pas als vader thuiskomt means we do not eat until father gets home.
When a Hoewel clause comes first, the main clause starts with its verb: ..., willen wij de film afkijken.
werken takes aan for the thing worked on: gewerkt aan het project means worked on the project.
het druk hebben is the idiom for being busy: zij heeft het druk means she is busy, literally 'has it busy'.
Most ordinals below twenty add -de to the number: drie becomes derde, 'third', as in de derde zaterdag.
herinneren is reflexive and needs ons here, so wij herinneren ons means 'we remember'.
Nadat pairs with the past perfect for the earlier event: nadat we de film hadden gezien, then the main clause follows.
For 'on which' about a thing, Dutch uses waarop, joining waar and op into one word: de dag waarop wij elkaar ontmoetten.
Anything traveling by water uses varen, not gaan: de boot vaart over het meer, the boat sails across.
Towns and places take liggen for their location: het dorp ligt tussen de bergen means the village lies between them.
'Born' uses zijn plus geboren: is vorige maand geboren means 'was born last month'.
Dutch says units before tens: zesennegentig is zes-en-negentig, literally 'six-and-ninety' for 96.
